articles.title: Ariel Reps Seller in Bronx Multifamily Portfolio
articles.narrative: Ariel Property Advisors has facilitated the sale of a three-building multifamily portfolio in the Bronx for $7.5 million. The portfolio, comprising 143 rent-stabilized apartments across 140,470 square feet, attracted strong buyer interest due to its scale and long-term upside potential in well-connected neighborhoods. The transaction underscores the sustained demand for multifamily assets in the Bronx, particularly those offering proximity to transit, retail, and institutional anchors.

data_points.address: 2460 Grand Ave. and 636-646 E. 231st St., Bronx, NY
data_points.notable_features: The portfolio includes one elevator building and two walk-up buildings, offering a mix of studio to three-bedroom apartments. It is located near major transit, retail corridors, and institutional anchors.

articles.title: Former Hotel-Turned-University-Campus Trades for Repositioning
articles.narrative: A former hotel that was converted into a university campus in Lancaster, CA, has been sold for $14.4 million. The buyer, 44049 Sierra Hwy Propco, LLC, plans to reposition the 87,598-square-foot property into a regional hub for community and social services in collaboration with Los Angeles County. The seller was University of Antelope Valley, LLC, which previously operated a private university on the site until its closure in 2024. The property's flexible layout and existing infrastructure were key factors in its suitability for a new mission-driven use.

data_points.notable_features: Originally developed as a hotel before being converted into a university campus.
data_points.project_notes: The property was acquired vacant and will be repositioned as a regional hub for community and social services in partnership with Los Angeles County.

articles.title: OPEN Impact Arranges 15-Year Occupancy for Brooklyn Charter School
articles.narrative: OPEN Impact Real Estate has arranged a 15-year lease for Launch Expeditionary Learning Charter School, securing approximately 77,000 square feet at 5902 Sixth Ave. in Brooklyn's Sunset Park. This transaction provides the charter school with a permanent, purpose-built educational campus, which is a rare find in the Brooklyn market. The school plans to relocate in July 2027 after facility modernizations.

data_points.notable_features: Purpose-built educational campus with a regulation-size gymnasium.
data_points.project_notes: The property was originally occupied by Our Lady of Perpetual Help Catholic Academy.

articles.title: Massachusetts Awards $15M in Tax Credits to Support 856 New Homes
articles.narrative: The Healey-Driscoll Administration has allocated $15.3 million in Commercial Conversion Tax Credits to five projects across Massachusetts, facilitating the transformation of vacant or underutilized commercial properties into 856 new rental homes. This initiative, part of the Affordable Homes Act signed in 2024, aims to revitalize downtowns and commercial districts by increasing housing supply and bringing new residents and economic activity to these areas. The projects include the adaptive reuse of a historic office building in Boston, a former retail building in Worcester, an obsolete hotel in Westford, historic buildings in Springfield, and commercial buildings in Dedham.

data_points.notable_features: Adaptive reuse of vacant or underutilized commercial properties into rental housing.
data_points.project_notes: Second round of awards through the Commercial Conversion Tax Credit Initiative, established by the Affordable Homes Act in 2024.

articles.title: City Realty Buys Brookline Multifamily Portfolio for $23M
articles.narrative: City Realty has acquired a nine-building multifamily portfolio in Brookline, MA, for $23.15 million. The portfolio comprises 49 residential units and three commercial spaces, totaling 65,262 square feet with a 95% occupancy rate. The properties attracted significant investor interest due to their prime location near major medical and academic institutions, with the potential for value creation through future unit renovations.

data_points.notable_features: Located near top medical and academic institutions in a desirable neighborhood; only 12% of units fully renovated and 57% partially upgraded, offering value-add potential.

articles.market_intelligence: The sale attracted nationwide interest from private and institutional investors, indicating strong demand for well-located multifamily assets in Greater Boston. Investor conviction in Brookline remains high despite uncertainty surrounding a proposed rent-control ballot initiative.

articles.title: Hackman Capital Sells El Segundo Flex Building For $27M
articles.narrative: Majestic Asset Management has acquired a flex building in El Segundo, CA, for $27 million from Hackman Capital Partners. The property is fully leased to a prominent electric vehicle manufacturer. This transaction marks a significant increase in value from its previous sale price of $15.3 million in 2018.

data_points.notable_features: Fully leased to an electric vehicle manufacturer.

articles.title: LA County Hotel-Turned-University Sells For $14.4M: The Los Angeles Deal Sheet
articles.narrative: The University of Antelope Valley has sold its campus property for $14.4 million. The buyer intends to redevelop the site into a regional hub, signaling a potential shift in the property's use from educational to a broader commercial or community function.

articles.title: Texas Governor's Data Center Power Pause Gets Split Verdict From Developers
articles.narrative: Texas Governor Greg Abbott's decision to pause new data center grid connections has elicited a mixed response from industry leaders. Some developers view the pause as a necessary measure to address grid stability and ensure long-term energy reliability, potentially leading to more sustainable growth. Others express concern that the moratorium could stifle the state's competitive edge in attracting new data center investment, potentially diverting projects to other states with more predictable energy policies. The debate highlights the tension between rapid industrial growth and the need for robust infrastructure planning.

articles.title: MAPPED: Dozens Of Properties Hit The Market As Prosecutors Circle Shabselses' Bankrupt Empire
articles.narrative: Approximately 50 properties are being marketed for sale as a family real estate business faces bankruptcy and ongoing legal challenges. The portfolio sale comes amidst the collapse of the real estate empire, with prosecutors reportedly investigating the firm's activities.

data_points.project_notes: Approximately 50 properties are being sold as part of a bankruptcy proceeding.

articles.title: Lenders Up Foreclosures On Financially Stressed U.S. Households In 2026
articles.narrative: Foreclosure filings across the U.S. increased by 21% in 2026, reflecting growing financial stress among households. This rise indicates a significant uptick in lenders initiating foreclosure proceedings against homeowners facing economic difficulties.
